newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: The weak bullion price -- failing to sustain its brief attempt at a rally and fixing at a 3-1/4 year low in London -- hammered away at South African gold stocks on Wednesday, dragging them lower but failing to force them to finish at the day's worst levels, dealers said.
"Golds were again under fire from bullion, but, although really weak, they managed to climb back off their lows," one dealer said.
The gold index finished 41.5 points weaker at 1,408.4.

With bullion looking unlikely to climb up and many commentators expecting it to continue weak, dealers said it was unlikely that gold shares would recover and that the next few days of trade were likely to be dull.
"Bullion failed to hold its brief rally and has dented sentiment for golds. We are going to see a few days of very dull trade in that market," a dealer said.
Analysts said that it was mainly foreign investors who were baling out of gold stocks and that locals were sitting quietly and holding their positions until fresh signals emerged.

"The lack of support for gold shares is really coming from overseas -- look at the volumes that are starting to come back from across the water," said Trevor Pearton, head of mining research at Societe Generale Frankel Pollak.
Industrial shares, on the other hand, enjoyed a fairly healthy day after initially disappointing the market by failing to jump on Wall Street's overnight strength.
Still the shares on that counter tripped down at the close of trade on profit-taking, finishing the industrial index 4.9 points firmer at 8,130.7.
"Industrials had a good day but at the death of trade they came off their best on profit-taking," a dealer said.

Dealers said that while underlying sentiment in the industrial market was positive, Mandela's rebuffing of the U.S. warning over the Syrian arms deal had taken some of the shine off the market's performance.
Dealers said that foreigners had re-entered the South African market after earlier pulling out on news of the proposed Syrian deal but that they remained cautious.
Dealers said that some consolidation was seen over the next few days. Institutions had given good support to trade throughout the day, they added.
Volumes were good and most interest was seen in smaller companies.
South African industrial equity futures contracts disappointed by failing to take advantage of Wall Street's overnight performance and instead slipping to levels below settlement.
Dealers said the industrial futures were seen coming off a tad more before moving higher.
Gold futures remained weighed by the weak bullion price but could recover to around 1,010 bid.
The near-term gold contract was at 1,000/005 from 1,033, the industrial contract was at 7,952/65 from 7,973 and the all-share contracts was at 6,250/70 from 6,270.
